hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: Traverse cell by cell starting from (0, 0) according to the directional character at each position.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: Track visited cells using an indicator matrix or timestamp step markers to detect cycles.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Stop and return the coordinates of the current cell when the next move steps outside grid boundaries or into a visited cycle.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def lastVisitedCell(grid: list[str]) -> list[int]:
    m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    dirs = {
        'R': (0, 1),
        'L': (0, -1),
        'D': (1, 0),
        'U': (-1, 0)
    }

    r, c = 0, 0
    visited = set()

    while True:
        visited.add((r, c))
        move = grid[r][c]
        dr, dc = dirs[move]
        nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc

        # Check if next step exits grid or enters a cycle
        if not (0 <= nr < m and 0 <= nc < n) or (nr, nc) in visited:
            return [r, c]

        r, c = nr, nc
```

complexity.notes: Simulation visits each cell at most once until boundary exit or cycle detection.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Without visited state tracking, infinite loops occur on cyclic grids.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Visited set stores at most m * n coordinate pairs.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Simulates grid path and handles termination conditions cleanly.
